primitives.name: Referee Authority Kernel

primitives.assumptions: Umpire decisions are subordinated to referee authority; precedence is transitive and reflexive.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When referee fails to acknowledge umpire penalty within 0.2 seconds of foul occurrence.

This is modeled mathematically as a partially ordered set (poset), where each rule section is a node and precedence relationships between sections are directed edges. Penalties associated with violations serve as weights on these edges, forming a weighted poset. The referee authority kernel operates as a derived function over this structure, enforcing precedence of umpire penalties through a transitive decision tree. The ignorance threshold function acts as an error metric, inversely related to rule comprehension, which degrades performance when exceeding critical thresholds. These primitives collectively define a dualistic system: one of structured regulation and one of cognitive failure, both influencing game dynamics through probabilistic decision paths.
